title: The art of listening
subject: Japanese jazz kissa
context: Imagine going somewhere specifically to listen to a record. Japan's jazz kissa turn carefully assembled record collections and sound systems into shared listening experiences. Somewhere between a café, a record collection and a sanctuary, these spaces make music the main event.

editorialNotes: House rules vary: the strictest kissa forbid talking, others allow conversation (National Geographic). The copy doesn't imply all are silent.
Numbers differ by period (800+ at the 1960s peak; about 400 today per National Geographic); the copy avoids counts.
